title: sparse-headroom-onramp-and-tenant-ferrying-prd-notes
summary: Sketch for a low-cost baseline headroom model (sparse headroom) that keeps small warm capacity distributed across dedicated pools and a lightweight ferrying mechanism to move short-lived capacity to tenants. Focus: reduce cold-start latency for bursts while preserving isolation and predictable billing.
background: We get two recurrent asks: (1) tenants want near-instant burst without paying for large reserved capacity; (2) platform must preserve isolation and predictable SLOs. Existing proposals (warm-pools, burst credits, soft-reserve) trade off cost or complexity. Sparse headroom is a hybrid: a thin always-on band of kernels/slots across nodes + a controlled ferry that attaches those slots to tenant runtime for short windows.
problem_statement: Cold starts for large models and unpredictable burst costs cause customers to overprovision reserved capacity or suffer degraded latency. Current burst-handling mechanisms either require large warm pools or aggressive preemption which harms isolation. Need: predictable latency for microbursts, bounded cost increase, minimal changes to infra/tenancy model.
goals: 1) Reduce p50/p95 burst latency by pre-attaching small fast-warm slots; 2) Limit cost delta relative to baseline reserved capacity (<10% incremental for typical customers); 3) Maintain tenant isolation guarantees via soft delegation and lease fences; 4) Operate with existing Dedicated pool orchestration with small infra changes.
non_goals: 1) Replace full warm pool designs for heavy sustained throughput; 2) Provide unlimited burst capacity (this is a smoothing/hedging layer); 3) Solve model-specific long cold compiles—assume models are pre-cached/compiled for common variants.
proposed_design: High level: create a sparse headroom layer composed of a fraction of slots on many machines (e.g., 2-5% of nodes carry 1-2 spare slots each). These slots are kept in a warm-but-light state (kept kernel loaded, KV cache minimal). A ferry controller grants a short lease to a tenant: the slot enters tenant execution context via a fast attach (resource proxying + token-handoff). Leases are time-boxed (30s-5m) with options for renewal. If contention arises, priority lanes enforce SLO-weighted reclamation. Preemption uses a soft-handoff: ferryed slot attempts graceful handover of KV cache to fallback model variant or to a queued request bucket.
components: 1) Sparse headroom allocator service (controller): tracks global spare slots, lease state, metrics. 2) Ferry attach protocol: secure token exchange and tenant identity binding. 3) Lease enforcement: TTL, renewal hooks, soft revoke callback. 4) Isolation guard: per-tenant fence and fallback routing. 5) Billing/ledger: micro-charge for ferryed minutes + potential credit usage for heavy consumers.
admission_and_policies: - Admission uses probabilistic reservation: tenants with committed lanes get a higher ferry success rate. - Soft quota: each tenant has daily ferry tokens (configurable per commitment). - Reclamation priority: urgent-slo tenants > committed > opportunistic. - Model compatibility checks: ferry only allowed for pre-approved model families to avoid binary incompatibilities.
telemetry_and_slo: Essential metrics: ferry_attach_latency(ms), ferry_success_rate(%), ferry_lease_renew_rate, reclaimed_lease_count, tenant_ferry_cost_delta, p50/p95 generation latency pre/post ferry. SLO targets: ferry_attach_latency p50<40ms p95<220ms; ferry_success_rate >= 95% for committed tenants; reclaimed_lease_count alarm if >1% of active leases over 1h.
cost_model_and_pricing: Two-part micropricing: (A) platform maintains sparse headroom pool cost centrally (amortized across tenants as a small percent surcharge), (B) tenants incur per-lease minute micro-charge for opportunistic usage and pay less for committed-tier ferry minutes. Rough estimate: a sparse band sized at 3% of fleet adds ~3-5% incremental infra cost but reduces tenant overcommit by ~15% in simulations. Need finance validation.
safety_and_isolation: - All ferry attach flows use scoped ephemeral credentials with limited privileges. - Tenant processes run in normal tenant sandbox after attach; network and data plane isolation same as regular dedicated lanes. - On preemption, ferry controller fails fast to tenant fallback route (dedicated fallback queue or lower-fidelity model variant). - Observability injects tenant labels for tracing and for automatic SLA reconciliation.
rollout_plan: Phase A (experiment): small fleet in 1 region, opt-in customers (5 pilot tenants). Measure attach latency, success, customer UX. Phase B (expanded beta): wider fleet, introduce billing ledger, add UI in console to show ferry usage. Phase C (GA): enable default for committed-tier tenants with configurable parameters and guardrails.
migration_and_rollback: - Migration is non-invasive: ferry pool created as parallel capacity; no changes to tenant config required for opt-in. - Rollback: drain leases, disable new attachments, evict opportunistic slots and reconcile ledger. - Backwards compatibility: teams can disable ferrying per-tenant via console toggle or API flag.
operational_playbook: Runbook highlights: - Alarm: ferry_attach_latency spike -> check allocator backlog, node kernel health, network latency. - High reclaimed lease rate -> inspect surge patterns, consider increasing sparse-band temporarily. - Billing mismatch complaints -> reconcile per-tenant ledger and refund policy. - Incident: failed soft-handovers causing 503s -> immediately disable ferry attach and revert to queued fallback.
open_questions: 1) Optimal sizing strategy: fixed percent vs demand-driven autoscale of sparse band? 2) How to price opportunistic minutes without disincentivizing usage? 3) KV state handover feasibility for large-context models—can we transfer enough to make attach useful? 4) Security review for token-handoff pattern. 5) Latency trade-offs: is 30s-5m lease sweet spot? Need experiments.
dependencies: infra-fleet-scheduling, auth-ephemeral-cred, billing-ledger, observability-tracing, model-onboarding (compatibility list)
decision_log: Initial decision: pursue soft-attach ferry idea as a low-risk experiment. Rejected: radical pre-copy of KV state between nodes (too complex). Next milestone: prototype ferry attach in canary cluster.
